domain_restrictions: Each w_i is a positive integer
S is graded by assigning deg(x_i)=w_i
Each g_i is homogeneous with respect to this grading
The sequence g_1,...,g_d is a regular sequence in S
The quotient is by the ideal generated by g_1 through g_d
Degrees e_i are the grading degrees of g_i; consistent with homogeneity (typically nonnegative in a weighted polynomial grading)
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: Given a weighted graded polynomial ring S equal to k[x_1,...,x_d] with deg(x_i)=w_i where k is a field, d is a nonnegative integer, and each w_i is a positive integer, suppose g_1,...,g_d is a homogeneous regular sequence in S such that deg(g_i)=e_i for each i. Then the graded Hilbert series of the quotient ring S modulo the ideal generated by g_1,...,g_d is equal to the product over i from 1 to d of (1 minus q to the e_i) divided by the product over i from 1 to d of (1 minus q to the w_i).
quantifier_order: Let d be a nonnegative integer
For all choices of positive integers w_1 through w_d
Define S as the graded polynomial ring with deg(x_i)=w_i
For all choices of homogeneous elements g_1 through g_d in S that form a regular sequence and satisfy deg(g_i)=e_i
Then the graded Hilbert series identity holds for the quotient S modulo the ideal generated by g_1 through g_d

witness_dependencies: The Hilbert series formula uses only the degrees e_i of the given regular sequence elements g_i; it does not depend on any other data about g_i beyond regularity and homogeneity
The grading weights w_i determine the denominator factors 1 minus q to the w_i
Indexing is aligned: g_i has degree e_i for the same i used for w_i

statement_nl: Let k be a field, let d be a nonnegative integer, let w_1,...,w_d be positive integers, and let S = k[x_1,...,x_d] be graded by deg(x_i)=w_i. If g_1,...,g_d is a homogeneous regular sequence in S and deg(g_i)=e_i for each i, then the graded Hilbert series of the quotient is Hilb_{S/(g_1,...,g_d)}(q) = prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(e_i)) / prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(w_i)).
